BindingTarget.description: What a delivery dispatches. `function_id` is any iii function — `harness::send` for a wake, anything else for a mechanical reaction. Strict: an unknown key (sub-agent fields such as `task`) is refused when the agent observes, never silently dropped.

event_into.description: JSON pointer where the event lands inside the payload (default `/event`).

payload.description: Payload template; the delivered event is injected into it at `event_into`.

ConditionSpec.description: One declared condition. Evaluated at fire time with the typed decision contract; ordinary iii functions, so a barrier or a claim is just a function someone wrote.

LifecycleRequest.description: The caller-settable half of a binding's lifecycle. Strict on purpose: an unknown key here (the retired `expires_at` above all) is a dropped deadline, so it must error naming the accepted fields, never pass.

expires_in_ms.description: Relative deadline: the observer stops this many milliseconds after it was created (the only deadline form).

max_fires.description: Lifetime delivery budget; the observer is removed on its Nth delivery.

once.description: Remove the observer after its first delivery (same as top-level `once`).

action.description: User-facing text saying what happened, shown with each delivery.

args.description: Args for the worker that hosts the function, a JSON object; its description says which it takes: cron `{ "expression" }`, database `{ "db", "table"?, "ops"? }`, `harness::on-timer` `{ "in_ms" }` or `{ "at" }` (epoch ms). Omit for a function that takes none.

conditions.description: Delivery-time gates, in order; each is an iii function answering `{ decision: "allow" | "skip", payload?, reason? }`.

filters.description: Which calls reach this observer, a JSON object of explicit operators on the call's fields: `{ "input.scope": { "$eq": "run" } }`.

function_id.description: The function to observe: `state::on-changed`, `cron::on-tick`, `harness::on-timer`, `database::on-row-changed`, or any other function. What it returns is the event.

label.description: A short human label echoed back in the notification text.

lifecycle.description: When the observer stops delivering; top-level `once` is the shorthand.

namespace.description: Where the function is hosted; omitted: this harness's namespace, then `default`, then Compose's.

once.description: Remove the observer after its first delivery; defaults to true for a wake (no `target`) and `harness::on-timer`, false for a call target and `cron::on-tick`.

target.description: The function called with each event: `{ function_id, payload?, event_into? }` — the fixed payload and the JSON pointer where the event is injected into it (default `/event`). Omit it to be notified in this session instead. `harness::spawn` is never a valid target.

note.description: Advisory only — the observer was CREATED, but its wiring looks suspicious (e.g. a filter naming a key someone already wrote). Read it and fix the wiring if it applies.

once.description: The effective `once` flag applied (after the per-function default).
